summary: The Bahamas combines a mixed ocean-and-land conservation programme with targeted ecosystem restoration. Its November 2024 debt conversion directs US$124 million in savings over 15 years to ocean protection, mangrove restoration and marine-park management. Conservation pledges designate 20% of land cover as forest reserves, protected forests or conservation forests; taking 20% of the 11,649 km² land area gives about 2,330 km², roughly 44% of the 5,322 km² currently mapped as forest. The marine-energy passages report two facility figures—up to three and five—for carbon-neutral marine protected-area facilities using photovoltaic rather than diesel systems. Restoration concentrates on re-establishing and rehabilitating 50 ha (0.5 km²) of Davis Creek on Andros, about 0.02% of current mapped wetland. The package links forest governance, carbon-neutral marine management and a focused mangrove-restoration pilot.
